subject: Computer Networking
title: Satellite Internet Constellations
description: Learn Satellite Internet Constellations in one minute.

hook.text: Starlink has 6,000+ satellites. They bring broadband to the most remote places on Earth.

buildup.text: LEO satellites orbit at 550 km, not 36,000. The closer orbit means much lower latency.

discovery.text: Starlink hits 25-60 ms latency. Geostationary takes 600 ms+. LEO feels like cable internet.

twist.text: Debris risk: a chain-reaction collision — Kessler Syndrome — could make LEO orbits unusable.

climax.text: Amazon Kuiper and OneWeb launch rival constellations. Competition cuts prices, expands coverage.

punchline.text: Satellite constellations bring broadband everywhere. The divide closes.

quiz.question: Why do LEO satellites provide lower latency than geostationary ones?
options: They orbit much closer to Earth, reducing signal travel distance
They use a faster communication protocol

details.summary: Low Earth orbit satellite constellations like Starlink and OneWeb deploy thousands of small satellites to provide broadband internet globally.
details.whyItMatters: Satellite constellations are closing the digital divide by bringing broadband to rural and remote areas where terrestrial infrastructure is impractical or uneconomical to build.
takeaways: LEO satellites orbit at 340 to 1,200 km for low latency
Thousands of satellites create continuous global coverage
Latency of 20 to 50 ms approaches fixed broadband performance

faq.question: How does Starlink achieve low latency?
faq.answer: Starlink satellites orbit at approximately 550 kilometers altitude, keeping the signal path short. Geostationary satellites at 36,000 kilometers create 600-millisecond round trips. LEO proximity reduces this to 20 to 50 milliseconds, making video calls and gaming feasible over satellite internet.

faq.question: What are the challenges of satellite internet?
faq.answer: Maintaining thousands of satellites requires constant replacement as they deorbit. Space debris is a growing concern. Weather and obstructions affect signal quality. Capacity is shared among users in an area. Regulatory coordination across countries adds complexity.
